body.statement: For the fixed nested midpoint refinement and the lexicographically tie-broken projections, \(\|x-p_{dj,h}(x)\|_2\le h\) on every \(C_{dj}\) and \(\|x-p_{B,h}(x)\|_2\le h\) on \(B\). Consequently every \(g_d\in\mathcal F_d\) yields a feasible nodal vector \(v_{d,h,z}=g_d(z)\), its cell and boundary pushforward errors are at most \(M_dh\), and \(U_d(m_d)\le B_{d,h}(m_d)\) for every \(m_d\in K_d\). For every compatible mean, \(B_{d,h}(m_d)\to U_d(m_d)\) as \(h\downarrow0\). For every atomic optimizer \(v_{d,h}\), the canonical extension satisfies \[\left\|A_d(E_{d,h}v_{d,h})-m_d\right\|_2\le2M_dh\sqrt{|J_d|},\qquad \left|\int_BE_{d,h}v_{d,h}\,d\nu-\sum_{z\in\mathcal N_h}v_{d,h,z}\nu_h(\{z\})\right|\le M_dh.\] If \(r_d(m_d)>0\), relative-interior endpoint stability gives \(U_d(A_dE_{d,h}v_{d,h})\le U_d(m_d)+\|A_dE_{d,h}v_{d,h}-m_d\|_2/r_d(m_d)\); adding the boundary projection error and the \(M_dh\) correction in \(B_{d,h}\) yields exactly \[0\le B_{d,h}(m_d)-U_d(m_d)\le2M_dh\left(1+\frac{\sqrt{|J_d|}}{r_d(m_d)}\right).\] The exact-moment piecewise-affine fiber is then nonempty for all sufficiently small \(h\), \(P_{d,h}(m_d)\le U_d(m_d)\), and \[0\le U_d(m_d)-P_{d,h}(m_d)\le\varepsilon_{d,h}\left(1+\frac{\sqrt{|J_d|}}{r_d(m_d)}\right),\qquad \varepsilon_{d,h}=O(\sqrt h).\] The reflected programs give the corresponding lower-endpoint bounds and shrinking a posteriori effect-set gaps when certified finite-program optimization errors vanish.
body.justification: The result separates universal value-side approximation from exact primal recovery and quantifies precisely where relative-interior slack repairs continuous moments.
body.gap: Mula and Nouy prove moment-hierarchy convergence, and Baldi and Mourrain quantify pseudo-moment approximation, but neither supplies this exact response-surface moment correction or its clipping-preserving endpoint gap.
body.consumer: A practitioner receives a monotonically valid outer interval at every compatible mean and a convergent exact-feasibility inner certificate away from exposed faces.
body.proof_tex:
We first use geometric projection and compactness for the universal outer
program.  Because \(\mathcal T_h\) conforms to every cell and to \(B\), each
point of a cell belongs to a triangle contained in that cell and each point of
\(B\) belongs to a boundary edge of the triangulation.  A vertex of that triangle
or edge is at Euclidean distance at most its diameter, hence at most \(h\).
Nearest-node projection and lexicographic tie breaking therefore give
\[
 \lVert x-p_{dj,h}(x)\rVert_2\leq h,
 \qquad
 \lVert x-p_{B,h}(x)\rVert_2\leq h.
\]
For \(g_d\in\mathcal F_d\), put \(v_{d,h,z}=g_d(z)\).  Its nodal range and every
pairwise Lipschitz inequality hold, and pushforward gives
\[
\begin{split}
\left|\sum_zv_{d,h,z}\mu_{dj,h}(\{z\})-m_{dj}\right|
&=\left|\int\{g_d(p_{dj,h}(x))-g_d(x)\}\,d\mu_{dj}(x)\right|\leq M_dh,\\
\left|\sum_zv_{d,h,z}\nu_h(\{z\})-\int_Bg_d\,d\nu\right|
&\leq M_dh.
\end{split}
\]
Applying this to a primal optimizer proves
\(U_d(m_d)\leq V_{d,h}(m_d)+M_dh\).  Since \(U_d\leq1\), clipping the latter
quantity at one preserves the inequality, so \(U_d(m_d)\leq B_{d,h}(m_d)\).

For any feasible nodal vector, pairwise feasibility implies that the McShane
formula equals the prescribed value at every node; clipping does not change
those values.  Its extension \(e_h=E_{d,h}v_{d,h}\) belongs to \(\mathcal F_d\),
and the preceding pushforward argument, now combined with the relaxed moment
constraint, gives
\[
 \lVert A_de_h-m_d\rVert_2\leq2M_dh\sqrt{|J_d|},
 \qquad
 \left|\int_Be_h\,d\nu-\sum_zv_{d,h,z}\nu_h(\{z\})\right|\leq M_dh.
\]
Take atomic optimizers along any sequence \(h\downarrow0\).  Their extensions
are uniformly bounded and equicontinuous, so a subsequence converges uniformly
to some \(e\in\mathcal F_d\).  The last display implies \(A_de=m_d\), and the
atomic objectives converge along this subsequence to \(\int_Be\,d\nu\leq U_d(m_d)\).
Together with the already proved outer inequality this yields
\(B_{d,h}(m_d)\to U_d(m_d)\) for every compatible mean, including boundary means.

We now use relative-hull support functions to obtain the quantitative bounds.
Let \(m=m_d\), \(r=r_d(m)>0\), and \(q=A_de_h\).  If \(q\neq m\), write
\(v=(q-m)/\lVert q-m\rVert_2\).  Since \(m-rv\in K_d\) and
\[
 m=\frac r{r+\lVert q-m\rVert_2}q
   +\frac{\lVert q-m\rVert_2}{r+\lVert q-m\rVert_2}(m-rv),
\]
concavity and \(0\leq U_d\leq1\) imply
\[
 U_d(q)\leq U_d(m)+\frac{\lVert q-m\rVert_2}{r}.
\]
For an atomic optimizer, its objective is at most
\(\int_Be_h\,d\nu+M_dh\leq U_d(q)+M_dh\).  Adding the final \(M_dh\) in
\(B_{d,h}\), and using the residual bound, proves exactly
\[
0\leq B_{d,h}(m)-U_d(m)
\leq2M_dh\left(1+\frac{\sqrt{|J_d|}}{r_d(m)}\right).
\]

For the inner program put \(K_{d,h}=A_d(\mathcal F_{d,h})\) and
\(\delta_h=\sqrt{|J_d|}\,\varepsilon_{d,h}\).  The finite nodal feasible set is
compact and convex.  Vertex range bounds extend over each triangle by
barycentricity, and integrating the bounded piecewise gradient along any segment
in convex \(S\) proves the global Euclidean Lipschitz bound.  Thus
\(\mathcal F_{d,h}\subseteq\mathcal F_d\) and \(K_{d,h}\) is compact and convex.
For every \(v\in E_d\),
uniformly approximating a support maximizer in \(\mathcal F_d\) gives
\[
 h_{K_{d,h}}(v)\geq h_{K_d}(v)-\delta_h\lVert v\rVert_2
 \geq v^\top m+(r_d(m)-\delta_h)\lVert v\rVert_2.
\]
If the ball \(m+(r_d(m)-\delta_h)\mathbb B_{E_d}\) were not contained in
\(K_{d,h}\), nearest-point separation inside \(m+E_d\) would contradict this
support inequality.  Hence the containment holds whenever \(\delta_h<r_d(m)\).

Let \(g^*\) attain \(U_d(m)\), and choose \(g_h\in\mathcal F_{d,h}\) with
\(\lVert g_h-g^*\rVert_\infty\leq\varepsilon_{d,h}\).  Write
\(e=A_dg_h-m\), so \(\lVert e\rVert_2\leq\delta_h\), and set
\(t=\delta_h/r_d(m)\).  If \(\delta_h=0\), \(g_h\) is already exactly feasible.
Otherwise
\[
 m-\frac{1-t}{t}e
 \in m+(r_d(m)-\delta_h)\mathbb B_{E_d}\subseteq K_{d,h}.
\]
Choose \(q_h\in\mathcal F_{d,h}\) with this moment and define
\(f_h=(1-t)g_h+tq_h\).  Then \(A_df_h=m\), and, using \(0\leq T(g^*),T(q_h)\leq1\),
\[
\begin{split}
 T(f_h)
 &\geq(1-t)\{U_d(m)-\varepsilon_{d,h}\}\\
 &\geq U_d(m)-\varepsilon_{d,h}-\frac{\delta_h}{r_d(m)}.
\end{split}
\]
Thus the exact-moment inner fiber is nonempty for all sufficiently small \(h\),
\(P_{d,h}(m)\leq U_d(m)\), and
\[
0\leq U_d(m)-P_{d,h}(m)
\leq\varepsilon_{d,h}\left(1+\frac{\sqrt{|J_d|}}{r_d(m)}\right).
\]

It remains to verify the asserted approximation rate rather than assume it.
Every child in a midpoint refinement is similar to its parent, so the finitely
many shapes in the initial triangulation give a uniform shape constant over all
levels.  For
\(M_d>0\), extend \(g\in\mathcal F_d\) to a clipped \(M_d\)-Lipschitz function
on \(\mathbb R^2\), let \(Z\) be standard Gaussian in \(\mathbb R^2\), and put
\(u_\delta(x)=\mathbb E[g(x+\delta Z)]\).  The radial density of
\(\lVert Z\rVert_2\) is \(re^{-r^2/2}\mathbf1\{r\geq0\}\), whose first moment is
\(\sqrt{\pi/2}\).  Direct coupling gives
\[
 \lVert u_\delta-g\rVert_\infty
 \leq M_d\delta\mathbb E\lVert Z\rVert_2
 =M_d\delta\sqrt{\pi/2}.
\]
Differentiating the convolution of the bounded weak gradient in a unit direction
and using
\(\mathbb E|Z_1|=2\int_0^\infty ze^{-z^2/2}dz/\sqrt{2\pi}=\sqrt{2/\pi}\)
gives
\[
 \lVert D^2u_\delta\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq \frac{M_d}{\delta}\mathbb E|Z_1|
 =\frac{M_d}{\delta}\sqrt{2/\pi}.
\]
Let \(I_hu_\delta\) be nodal affine interpolation.  If \(R_T\) has as rows the
two edge vectors of triangle \(T\), midpoint shape regularity makes
\(C=\sup_T h_T\lVert R_T^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}/\sqrt2<\infty\).  Taylor's
formula on the two edges and barycentric interpolation then give
\[
 \lVert\nabla I_hu_\delta\rVert_2\leq M_d(1+\theta),\qquad
 \lVert I_hu_\delta-u_\delta\rVert_\infty\leq M_dh,
 \qquad
 \theta=C\sqrt{2/\pi}\,h/\delta.
\]
The contraction
\[
 q_h=\frac12+\frac{I_hu_\delta-1/2}{1+\theta}
\]
is in \(\mathcal F_{d,h}\), preserves the range, and satisfies
\[
 \lVert q_h-g\rVert_\infty
 \leq M_d\delta\sqrt{\pi/2}+M_dh+\theta/2.
\]
Taking \(\delta=\sqrt h\) proves
\(\varepsilon_{d,h}=O(\sqrt h)\), with a constant depending only on the fixed
shape-regular initial mesh and \(M_d\).  When \(M_d=0\), constants are represented
exactly and \(\varepsilon_{d,h}=0\).  Finally, applying every construction to
\(1-g\) at moment \(\mathbf1-m_d\) gives the lower-endpoint programs.  Combining
the two armwise outward and inward endpoint errors gives the claimed shrinking
a posteriori effect-set gaps whenever the finite-program optimization errors
also vanish.
